concepts.name: Points, lines, and planes
concepts.summary: Recall and describe points, lines, rays, segments and planes and name them with correct notation.

concepts.name: Angle types and measurement
concepts.summary: Classify angles as acute, right, obtuse or straight and measure them in degrees with a protractor.

concepts.name: Parallel and perpendicular lines
concepts.summary: Explain what makes two lines parallel or perpendicular and recognise them in figures.

concepts.name: Triangle and quadrilateral classification
concepts.summary: Name triangles by sides and angles and quadrilaterals by their defining properties.

concepts.name: Perimeter and area formulas
concepts.summary: Recall perimeter and area formulas for rectangles, squares and triangles and state units.

concepts.name: Circle parts and vocabulary
concepts.summary: Identify radius, diameter, chord, circumference and center of a circle.

misconceptions.text: A square is not a rectangle because rectangles must have unequal sides.
Area and perimeter measure the same thing and use the same units.
A triangle's height is always one of its sides.

concepts.name: Angle pair relationships
concepts.summary: Use complementary, supplementary, linear pair and vertical angle relationships to find unknown angles.

concepts.name: Transversal angle relationships
concepts.summary: Apply corresponding, alternate interior and same-side interior angle facts to parallel lines cut by a transversal.

concepts.name: Triangle angle sum
concepts.summary: Use the 180° angle sum and exterior angle theorem to find missing triangle angles.

concepts.name: Pythagorean theorem application
concepts.summary: Compute a missing side of a right triangle and test whether side lengths form a right triangle.

concepts.name: Polygon angle sums
concepts.summary: Find interior and exterior angle sums and individual angles of regular polygons.

concepts.name: Area of composite figures
concepts.summary: Compute areas of parallelograms, trapezoids, circles and composite shapes by decomposition.

concepts.name: Volume of prisms and cylinders
concepts.summary: Calculate volume as base area times height for prisms and cylinders.

misconceptions.text: Alternate interior angles are equal whether or not the lines are parallel.
The Pythagorean theorem a²+b²=c² works for any triangle.
Volume is found by multiplying all the side lengths of any solid.

concepts.name: Triangle congruence criteria
concepts.summary: Choose and apply SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS and HL to establish that two triangles are congruent.

concepts.name: Two-column proof construction
concepts.summary: Build a logically ordered proof with statements justified by givens, definitions, postulates and theorems.

concepts.name: CPCTC use in proofs
concepts.summary: Use congruent triangles to deduce equality of corresponding segments and angles.

concepts.name: Similar triangles and proportions
concepts.summary: Establish similarity by AA, SAS or SSS similarity and set up proportions for missing lengths.

concepts.name: Scale factor effects
concepts.summary: Predict how scale factor k changes lengths, areas (k²) and volumes (k³).

concepts.name: Circle arcs and central angles
concepts.summary: Relate central and inscribed angles to arcs and compute arc length and sector area.

concepts.name: Surface area of solids
concepts.summary: Compute surface area and volume of prisms, cylinders, cones and spheres using nets and formulas.

concepts.name: Special right triangles
concepts.summary: Use the side ratios of 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 triangles to find lengths without the full theorem.

misconceptions.text: SSA is a valid triangle congruence criterion.
Doubling a figure's side lengths doubles its area.
CPCTC can be used to prove the triangles congruent in the first place.

concepts.name: Circle chord and tangent theorems
concepts.summary: Analyse relationships among chords, tangents and secants, including tangent-radius perpendicularity and segment product rules.

concepts.name: Strategy selection in proofs
concepts.summary: Analyse a problem to choose between congruence, similarity, angle chasing or auxiliary lines and plan a proof.

concepts.name: Auxiliary constructions
concepts.summary: Judge which added segments, parallels or altitudes will expose usable relationships in a figure.

concepts.name: Similarity in right triangles
concepts.summary: Derive and apply geometric mean relationships created by the altitude to the hypotenuse.

concepts.name: Cyclic quadrilateral properties
concepts.summary: Use opposite-angle supplementarity and inscribed angle results to analyse figures within circles.

concepts.name: Multi-step solid measurement
concepts.summary: Evaluate approaches to volume and surface area of composite solids, including slant heights and cross sections.

concepts.name: Proof validity assessment
concepts.summary: Evaluate proofs for gaps, unjustified assumptions, circular reasoning and diagram-based conclusions.

misconceptions.text: A conclusion that looks true in an accurate diagram needs no justification.
A tangent line to a circle can intersect the circle at two points.
Any quadrilateral can be inscribed in a circle.

concepts.name: Axiomatic structure of Euclid
concepts.summary: Evaluate how theorems depend on postulates, especially the parallel postulate, and judge the logical order of results.

concepts.name: Non-Euclidean contrasts
concepts.summary: Assess which Euclidean results fail on spheres or hyperbolic planes, such as the triangle angle sum.

concepts.name: Original proof design
concepts.summary: Create proofs for unfamiliar statements and compare multiple proofs, such as synthetic, coordinate and transformational, for efficiency.

concepts.name: Coordinate and transformation methods
concepts.summary: Design coordinate or rigid-motion arguments that prove congruence and similarity results.

concepts.name: Geometric construction design
concepts.summary: Devise and justify compass-and-straightedge constructions and recognise impossible ones such as trisecting an arbitrary angle.

concepts.name: Modeling with geometric measures
concepts.summary: Build and critique geometric models of real situations, choosing approximations and judging error in area and volume estimates.

concepts.name: Teaching geometric reasoning
concepts.summary: Evaluate learner arguments and sequence tasks to diagnose and repair reasoning errors in geometry.

misconceptions.text: Euclidean geometry is the only consistent geometry and describes physical space exactly.
Any angle can be trisected with compass and straightedge given enough ingenuity.
A proof that works for one drawn example is sufficient to establish a general theorem.
